rationale: A 46-year-old HIV-infected male evaluated for ring-enhancing brain lesions and adrenal mass. Serology for Taenia solium was negative, and adrenal mass aspirate confirmed Nocardia spp., establishing disseminated nocardiosis and ruling out neurocysticercosis.

evidence_items.source_quote: Blood, urine, and stool cultural exams were negative, as well as Schistosoma spp. and Taenia solium serology.

rationale: A 40-year-old male presenting with visual loss and brain lesions. Infectious etiologies including cysticercosis and tuberculosis were considered. Brain biopsy revealed necrotizing granulomatous inflammation with acid-fast bacilli and positive M. tuberculosis culture, excluding cysticercosis.

evidence_items.source_quote: possibility of an infiltrative optic neuropathy due to an infectious (tuberculosis, cysticercosis) or inflammatory condition (sarcoidosis) was considered most likely.

rationale: A 39-year-old male presenting with a unilateral free-floating vitreous cyst. Serology for cysticercosis was explicitly tested and negative, ruling out ocular and neurocysticercosis.

evidence_items.source_quote: Blood serology tests were negative for Toxoplasma gondii, Toxocara canis, cysticercosis and Echinococcus.

rationale: A 78-year-old male evaluated for a floating vitreous cyst. Blood serology tests for cysticercosis were negative, ruling out cysticercosis.

evidence_items.source_quote: Blood serology tests were negative for Toxoplasma gondii, Toxocara canis, cysticercosis and Echinococcus.

rationale: A 14-year-old male with a posterior vitreous cyst. Blood serology for cysticercosis was normal/negative, and brain magnetic resonance showed no pathological findings.

evidence_items.source_quote: The clinical assessment comprised a physical examination, blood tests, including a hemogram, serology for Toxoplasma gondi, Toxocara, Echinococcosis and cysticercosis, and a blood cell count for eosinophils. All of the blood tests were normal.

rationale: A 51-year-old male with multiple sclerosis presenting with deterioration. Neurocysticercosis was evaluated in the differential diagnosis, but negative CSF analysis and serology explicitly argued against and ruled out neurocysticercosis.

evidence_items.source_quote: The negative results of the CSF analysis and serology argued against a neurocysticercosis, lymphoma, or PML.

rationale: A 38-year-old male with stroke secondary to invasive fungal sinusitis (mucormycosis). Neurocysticercosis was considered in the differential diagnosis of CSF eosinophilic pleocytosis but ruled out, as biopsy confirmed Rhizopus fungal infection.

evidence_items.source_quote: Parasitic infections such as strongyloidiasis or neurocysticercosis may give a similar clinical picture with eosinophilic CSF pleocytosis. However, he had always lived in Los Angeles and Arizona without traveling further afield and without a history of consuming raw snails or exotic foods. Therefore, parasitic infection was unlikely given his social history, negative travel history, and lack of risk factors.

rationale: A 47-year-old male presenting with seizures and neurological deterioration found to have Glioblastoma Multiforme (GBM). Neurocysticercosis was a remote past infection 2 years prior that was treated and healed, not the active diagnosis.

evidence_items.source_quote: His medical history revealed that he had NC 2 years back [Figure 1a and b], for which he received a course of antihelmenthics (Albendazole) and advised antiepileptic (Phenytoin).

rationale: A 45-year-old male with a retroperitoneal paraaortic mass found to be pseudotumoral schistosomiasis. Infectious serology for Taenia solium IgG was negative.

evidence_items.source_quote: Ag HBs; Ac HBc T; HIV 1 + 2; Toxoplasma gondii; Entamoeba histolytica; Echinococcus granulosus; Taenia solium (IgG); Leishmania spp.; strongyloides and schistosoma. All results were negative and do not

rationale: A 67-year-old female presenting with frontotemporal dementia. Neurocysticercosis was diagnosed in childhood (56 years earlier) and is currently represented solely by inactive, non-viable calcified parenchymal scars on CT without active disease.

evidence_items.source_quote: The patient presented radiographic signs of calcified NCC on CT Scan (Figure 1). The predominant finding was more than 20 calcified lesions located bilaterally in the brain cortex and sub-cortical regions.

rationale: A 63-year-old male with ALK-rearranged NSCLC presenting with cystic brain lesions. Neurocysticercosis was considered in the differential diagnosis; CSF ELISA, fundoscopy, and Western blot were all negative, and lesions responded to ceritinib.

evidence_items.source_quote: The patient underwent investigation for neurocysticercosis with cerebrospinal fluid enzyme linked immunosorbent assay, fundoscopic examination and western blot, all of which resulted negative.
evidence_items.test_name: CSF ELISA and Western blot for NCC

rationale: A 78-year-old male presenting with a right trapezius neck mass. MRI raised a differential diagnosis of neurocysticercosis versus fibromatosis; open biopsy and histology confirmed fibromatosis, excluding cysticercosis.

evidence_items.source_quote: MRI again was reported with a differential of neurocysticercosis or fibromatosis.

rationale: An 8-year-old female presenting with severe hypereosinophilia and stroke diagnosed with eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis (EGPA). Blood serology to exclude Taenia solium was negative.

evidence_items.source_quote: Serology of the blood was performed to exclude parasitic diseases (toxoplasma, toxocara, taenia solium, trichinella or echinococcus), and cryptococcus antigens in the blood were excluded.

rationale: A 33-year-old male presenting with seizures and multiple intracranial masses. While cysticercosis IgG ELISA was positive due to known cestode serological cross-reactivity, metagenomic NGS of CSF detected 161 reads of Echinococcus multilocularis, proving Alveolar Echinococcosis and ruling out NCC.

evidence_items.source_quote: Serological evaluation of multiple parasite antigen by ELISA were applied. Cysticercosis Immunoglobulin G (IgG) and liver hydatid IgG antibody were both positive.

rationale: A 22-year-old female presenting with severe rhabdomyolysis and idiopathic eosinophilic polymyositis. Taenia solium was noted in the differential discussion as clinically unlikely given absence of neurological symptoms.

evidence_items.source_quote: While Toxoplasma and Taenia solium were not specifically tested for by serology, our patient did not display gastrointestinal or neurological symptoms to support these pat

rationale: A 19-year-old primigravida presenting with postpartum seizures and passage of a tapeworm. Head CT planned to evaluate for suspected neurocysticercosis revealed bilateral occipital hypodensities diagnosing PRES, excluding NCC.

evidence_items.source_quote: Computed tomography (CT) scan was planned keeping the diagnosis of neurocysticercosis in mind. However CT head revealed hypodensities in bilateral occipital lobe which the radiologist diagnosed as PRES.

rationale: A 24-year-old male with leukoencephalopathy, cerebral calcifications, and pontine cyst (LCC). Cysticercosis serology was negative, and cyst biopsy confirmed LCC pathology (Rosenthal fibers and eosinophilic granular bodies), excluding cysticercosis.

evidence_items.source_quote: Serologic study for cysticercosis was negative.

rationale: A 23-year-old male presenting with seizures and multiple ring-enhancing brain lesions. Serology at autopsy was negative for cysticercosis; postmortem brain examination confirmed tuberculous thrombophlebitis with acid-fast bacilli.

evidence_items.source_quote: IgG/IgM antibody to Mycobacterium tuberculosis, Toxoplasma gondii and Cysticercosis.

rationale: A 30-year-old male presenting with seizures and ring-enhancing brain lesions. Cysticercosis was considered in the differential diagnosis and tested negative on serology at autopsy; tuberculous thrombophlebitis was confirmed.

evidence_items.source_quote: negative for cysticercosis and toxoplasmosis.

rationale: A 35-year-old male presenting with endophthalmitis and cystic-enhancing cerebral lesions. Neurocysticercosis was considered in differential diagnosis; brain biopsy confirmed Nocardia multiloculated abscess, ruling out NCC.

evidence_items.source_quote: Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) of the brain [Figure 1a and b] showed multiple cystic-enhancing lesions over both cerebral hemispheres, suggestive of tuberculomas or neurocysticercosis.

rationale: A 39-year-old female presenting with a subconjunctival cystic lesion after retinal detachment surgery. Cysticercosis was listed in differential diagnosis; echography proved migrated silicone oil from previous surgery, ruling out cysticercosis.

evidence_items.source_quote: In the upper nasal quadrant a dome shaped lesion was detected, which arose with a differential diagnosis with scleral buckling extrusion, tumor, dermoid, ocular cysticercosis, and abscess (Figure 1(a)).

rationale: A 60-year-old male presenting with expressive aphasia and nonconvulsive status epilepticus. Neurocysticercosis antibodies in the diagnostic encephalopathy panel were negative, and patient was confirmed to have Creutzfeldt-Jakob Disease (CJD).

evidence_items.source_quote: neurocysticercosis antibodies, and an autoimmune and paraneoplastic panel.

rationale: A 46-year-old male evaluated for a spinal inflammatory mass. Testing for neurocysticercosis antibody was negative; diagnosis of spinal syphilitic gumma was confirmed by positive TPPA and RPR with cure on penicillin.

evidence_items.source_quote: tuberculosis antibody, neurocysticercosis antibody, and tumor marker.

rationale: A 49-year-old female evaluated for chronic eosinophilic pneumonia. Infectious disease serologies including cysticercosis were negative, confirming drug/radiation-induced eosinophilic pneumonia.

evidence_items.source_quote: cysticercosis, and trichinella spiralis was negative.

rationale: A 44-year-old female presenting with a spinal intramedullary mass confirmed as Candida albicans abscess. Serology for cysticercosis was non-reactive, ruling out neurocysticercosis.

evidence_items.source_quote: cysticercosis, human immunodeficiency virus (HIV), and human T-lymphotropic virus were not reactive

rationale: A 38-year-old female presenting with bilateral blind eyes due to intraocular echinococcosis. Cysticercosis ELISA IgG was negative (0.2), ruling out cysticercosis.

evidence_items.source_quote: cysticercosis ELISA IgG negative value of 0.2

rationale: An 11-year-old male initially empirically treated for presumed ocular cysticercosis of the medial rectus muscle. Excision biopsy and histopathological examination revealed an intramuscular cavernous hemangioma, ruling out cysticercosis.

evidence_items.source_quote: The histopathological examination revealed an intramuscular cavernous hemangioma (Figure 4).

rationale: A 26-year-old male with hydrocephalus who initially had a VP shunt placed for suspected neurocysticercosis without clinical response. CSF fungal culture and galactomannan confirmed Aspergillus terreus chronic meningitis and mycotic aneurysm, excluding neurocysticercosis.

evidence_items.source_quote: A ventriculoperitoneal shunt was installed for suspicion of neurocysticercosis. Even though treatment was initiated, there was no clinical improvement.

rationale: A 30-year-old male presenting with new-onset seizures and brain masses on MRI evaluated for infectious etiologies including cysticercosis. Cysticercosis serology was negative, and repeat surgical pathology along with antigen testing confirmed Cryptococcus.

evidence_items.source_quote: Numerous laboratory examinations, including HIV, rapid plasma reagin, toxoplasma immunoglobulin G and immunoglobulin M, Lyme, cytomegalovirus, tuberculosis, cysticercosis, and Echinococcus serology, were all negative.

rationale: A 76-year-old male with multiple myeloma presenting with altered mental status and brain ring-enhancing lesions with eccentric target signs. The differential diagnosis included neurocysticercosis, but the lesions were pathognomonic for cerebral toxoplasmosis.

evidence_items.source_quote: The clinical and radiographic differential also included primary central nervous system (CNS) lymphoma or other CNS infections such as CNS tuberculosis, CNS cryptococcosis, and neurocysticercosis.

rationale: A 10-year-old female presenting with refractory status epilepticus. Comprehensive diagnostic workup including CSF cysticercosis antibodies was negative, and trio whole exome sequencing identified a de novo pathogenic CACNA1A variant.

evidence_items.source_quote: Extensive diagnostic workup was pursued throughout the patient's course of treatment. These tests included serum acylcarnitine, ceruloplasmin, CRP, pyruvic acid, and vitamin D levels; cerebrospinal fluid lactic acid, cysticercosis antibodies, and amino acids; and genetic anomalies including mitochondrial disorders, Factor V Leiden genetic mutation, prothrombin time gene mutations, an epilepsy gene panel, a female febrile epilepsy panel, an SCN1A large deletion/duplication test, and chromosomal microarray, all of which were negative.

rationale: A 51-year-old woman admitted with severe hemolytic anemia and arsenic poisoning resulting from prolonged ingestion of traditional Chinese medicines. Her neurocysticercosis diagnosis occurred 12 years prior and was not the active condition evaluated during this admission.

evidence_items.source_quote: Twelve years before the admission, she had been diagnosed as neurocysticercosis with intermittent seizure attacks.

rationale: A 20-year-old female presenting with generalized tonic-clonic seizures and multiple ring-enhancing brain lesions evaluated for tuberculoma vs neurocysticercosis. Histopathology demonstrated necrotizing granulomas compatible with tuberculosis, and follow-up MRI confirmed resolution on anti-tuberculosis therapy.

evidence_items.source_quote: Two months after the onset of anti-tuberculosis therapy, follow-up cranial MRI showed near-complete resolution of the tuberculomas in the brain (Fig. 2).

rationale: A 20-year-old male presenting with headache, vision loss, hemiparesis, and ring-enhancing brain lesions evaluated for neurocysticercosis. Biopsy and infectious studies were negative, and he was diagnosed with Neuro-Behcet syndrome based on recurrent ulcers and steroid responsiveness.

evidence_items.source_quote: At this point, additional differential diagnoses were considered, including neurocysticercosis, autoimmune encephalitis, vasculitis, and multiple sclerosis among others.

rationale: A 71-year-old immunosuppressed male presenting with headache and a cerebellar ring-enhancing lesion evaluated for neurocysticercosis. Biopsy and culture demonstrated acid fast bacilli confirming cerebellar tuberculous abscess, and lesions regressed under anti-tuberculosis therapy.

evidence_items.source_quote: Differential diagnosis included pyogenic abscess (bacterial or fungal), neurocysticercosis, cystic glioma, or other cystic malignant/metastatic process.

rationale: A 43-year-old female presenting with repeated fever and space-occupying hepatic lesions evaluated with comprehensive parasite serologies. ELISA for cysticercosis IgG antibodies was negative, and liver biopsy/mNGS established hepatic fascioliasis/parasitic liver disease.

evidence_items.source_quote: The serum parasite IgG antibody, including schistosome, paragonimiasis, cysticercosis, trichinella spiralis, liver fluke, sparganosis, and hydatid IgG antibody detected by ELISA were negative on hospital day 12.

rationale: A 35-year-old male presenting with acute abdominal pain and a large left hypochondrium mass diagnosed as adrenal neuroblastoma. Neurocysticercosis is mentioned solely as a past medical history comorbidity under medication, with no active neurocysticercosis evaluated or diagnosed during this hospitalization.

evidence_items.source_quote: A 35-year-old male with history of neurocysticercosis under medication presented to the surgery department with left upper abdominal pain and lump of one-week duration.

rationale: A 25-year-old male presenting with headaches, diplopia, and a brainstem mass. Serum parasite ELISA testing was negative for cysticercosis but positive for Schistosoma japonicum, and rectal biopsy confirmed S. japonicum eggs, establishing cerebral schistosomiasis.

evidence_items.source_quote: A blood sample enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay for parasite antibody IgG was positive for S. japonicum and negative for fascioliasis, toxocariasis, trichinellosis, cysticercosis, echinococcosis, and sparganosis.

rationale: A 40-year-old male presenting with hemiparesis and multiple bilateral cystic brain lesions empirically treated for neurocysticercosis. Cysticercosis antibodies were negative, and craniotomy biopsy proved high-grade glioblastoma, ruling out neurocysticercosis.

evidence_items.source_quote: Despite cysticercosis antibodies being tested negative, the patient was also initiated on albendazole, praziquantel, and levetiracetam for the empiric treatment of neurocysticercosis and seizure prophylaxis.

rationale: A patient with remote childhood neurocysticercosis presenting with an intraventricular cystic lesion. Neuroendoscopic surgery revealed an inactive intraventricular fibrotic cyst with explicit absence of active neurocysticercosis.

evidence_items.source_quote: During the neurosurgery, an intraventricular fibrotic cyst was found and fenestrations were made to reestablish CSF flow. No evidence of active neurocysticercosis was found (Figure 5).

rationale: A 26-year-old male presenting with ptosis, meningeal signs, and ring-enhancing brain lesions evaluated for neurocysticercosis. Cysticercosis IgG was negative, CSF PCR detected M. tuberculosis, and the lesions responded to antitubercular therapy, establishing CNS tuberculomas.

evidence_items.source_quote: Cysticercosis immunoglobulin G level was found to be 0.9 ( >1.1 ng dl-1 is considered positive).

rationale: A male patient with remote craniotomy for neurocysticercosis in Mexico presenting with bilateral parotid masses presumed to be cysticercosis. Parotid biopsy and excision confirmed bilateral Warthin tumors, with no active neurocysticercosis.

evidence_items.source_quote: He had a history of neurocysticercosis, presumably owing to ingestion of uncooked pork in Mexico and had undergone a previous craniotomy with removal of the brain mass in Mexico.

rationale: A 60-year-old woman presenting with transient global amnesia due to an acute ischemic infarction of the left fornix. Head CT showed scattered intraparenchymal calcifications consistent with old inactive neurocysticercosis with no acute neurocysticercosis activity.

evidence_items.source_quote: Head CT without IV contrast showed scattered intraparenchymal calcifications consistent with old neurocysticercosis, and no acute abnormalities.

rationale: A 74-year-old male with life-long epilepsy historically assumed to be neurocysticercosis admitted with acute intracerebral hemorrhage. Dermatologic histopathology and brain vascular findings established blue rubber bleb nevus syndrome with cavernous-like vascular malformations, ruling out neurocysticercosis as the etiology.

evidence_items.source_quote: He was diagnosed with structural epilepsy suspected to be secondary to intraparenchymal neurocysticercosis and received a single course of albendazole.

rationale: A 45-year-old male with a history of epilepsy previously diagnosed with CNS neurocysticercosis. Evaluation of skin lesions and brain MRI confirmed familial blue rubber bleb nevus syndrome with cerebral cavernous malformation-like lesions, ruling out neurocysticercosis.

evidence_items.source_quote: The son of the previous patient (Case 1) was a 45-year-old male with a past medical history of epilepsy, diagnosed with CNS neurocysticercosis.

rationale: A patient evaluated for cysticercosis in whom brain CT, serum IgG ELISA, and stool examinations were performed, and neurocysticercosis was explicitly ruled out.

evidence_items.source_quote: Stool examination, ELISA for serum antibodies (IgG) and CT scan brain was done, and neurocysticercosis was ruled out.
evidence_items.test_name: Brain CT, serum ELISA IgG & stool examination

rationale: A 28-year-old female presenting with multiple brain lesions evaluated for neurocysticercosis. Diagnostic workup for neurocysticercosis was negative, and CSF 16S rRNA PCR confirmed Streptococcus intermedius bacterial brain abscesses.

evidence_items.source_quote: The diagnostic workup was negative for Mycobacterium tuberculosis, toxoplasmosis, neurocysticercosis, HIV, histoplasmosis, cryptococcosis, blastomycosis, and free-living amoebas.

rationale: An HIV-positive patient presenting with brain calcifications and recurrent perilesional edema evaluated for neurocysticercosis. EITB transfer blot for cysticercosis was negative, and the lesions represented late reactive perilesional edema following treated cerebral toxoplasmosis.

evidence_items.source_quote: Serum enzyme-linked immunoelectrodifusion transfer blot for cysticercosis was negative.

rationale: A female patient with a multiloculated cystic brain lesion evaluated for neurocysticercosis. Negative serology and absence of typical ring-enhancing features excluded neurocysticercosis, confirming dilated/ectatic Virchow-Robin spaces (VRS).

evidence_items.source_quote: However, negative serology for cysticercosis, combined with the absence of typical features such as ring-enhancing cysts, excluded this diagnosis.

rationale: A 43-year-old male with remote neurocysticercosis treated 2.5 years prior presenting with cognitive decline and hemiparesis. Brain MRI and pathology demonstrated a collision tumor of high-grade glioblastoma and meningioma with old calcified granulomas, without active neurocysticercosis.
step4_condition_matched: Neurocysticercosis (historical treated episode with inactive calcifications)

evidence_items.source_quote: His medical history included an episode of NCC, treated 21/2 years back with albendazole 15 mg/kg over 4 weeks 1 month; no concurrent medical conditions or relevant family history was reported at presentation.

rationale: A female patient presenting with feigned quadriplegia and self-reported remote history of neurocysticercosis in Thailand. Extensive evaluations and unmasking of fabricated imaging reports confirmed Munchausen syndrome / factitious disorder, with no evidence of neurocysticercosis.

evidence_items.source_quote: Additionally, she reported being diagnosed with neurocysticercosis after a trip to Thailand eight years prior.

rationale: A 24-year-old female presenting with headaches and focal seizures initially misdiagnosed with neurocysticercosis on outside MRI. CSF IgG for Taenia solium was negative, chest radiography demonstrated miliary infiltrates, and CBNAAT confirmed miliary tuberculosis with CNS tuberculomas.

evidence_items.source_quote: Final diagnosis: Miliary tuberculosis with CNS tuberculomas, initially misdiagnosed as neurocysticercosis.
evidence_items.target_concept: Miliary tuberculosis with CNS tuberculomas vs NCC

rationale: A 34-year-old female with Fanconi anemia presenting with cognitive deficits and widespread intracranial calcifications considered for neurocysticercosis. Infectious workup was negative and lack of travel history ruled out neurocysticercosis, confirming primary/genetic intracranial calcifications.

evidence_items.source_quote: Notably, imaging reports listed neurocysticercosis as a potential etiology for cerebral calcifications, but infectious disease workup was unremarkable, and the patient had not traveled outside of the United States.
